b_abstract_10.1016/j.concog.2015.02.006_.content: Top-down attention interacts with stimulus saliency in visual processing (fMRI). Inferior frontal junction and dorsal parietal regions integrate bottom-up and top-down control signals. EBA modulated by attention only at intermediate saliency.

b_abstract_10.1016/j.neuroimage.2025.121.content: Spider phobia (vs healthy controls) -> Increased resting-state multiscale entropy in limbic regions, especially BNST (7T MRI, n=73). BNST MSE positively correlated with phobia severity. Supports excessive intra-regional processing in anxiety.

b_abstract_10.1016/j.plaphy.2025.110154_.content: Biophilic plant design (lush greenery) -> Enhanced well-being by connecting humans to nature. Study tested nano-fertilizer to maintain plant attractiveness under nutrient stress for space applications.

b_abstract_10.1038/s41598-024-52908-5_1.content: Chronic critical illness (COVID) post-discharge -> Prevalence of fatigue (55%), anxiety (42%), depression (40%) remained high at 12 months. Limited health-related quality of life (EQ-5D-5L: 0.63). n=97.

b_abstract_10.1038/s41598-025-19113-4_1.content: Virtual plants in VR office environment -> No effect on path steering performance (NULL finding). Study challenges previous positive findings on biophilic design + cognition.

b_abstract_10.1038/s41598-025-95771-8_1.content: University common space characteristics -> Psychological restoration (n=630, 11 universities, Guangzhou). Direct effects: architectural scale/aesthetics, landscape richness, rest facilities, activity facilities. Mediators: nature contact, physical activity, social interaction.

b_abstract_10.1038/s41598-025-95771-8_2.content: Four patterns for high psychological restoration in university spaces: (1) integrated environment+facilities, (2) static rest patterns, (3) dynamic exercise patterns, (4) interaction-driven patterns. fsQCA analysis.

b_abstract_10.1080/00994480.2002.1074839.content: Daylight presence in classrooms -> Higher student academic performance. Multivariate regression across 3 US school districts. Authors suggest transferability to offices.

b_abstract_10.1080/07448481.2023.2252931.content: Green space exposure (outdoor garden, indoor plants, or nature posters) -> Decline in tension and fatigue in college students (n=79). Effect present in all conditions but less pronounced in office without greenery.

b_abstract_10.1080/17508975.2020.1732859.content: Indoor plants in office -> Improved perceived attention (p<0.05, n=40). Quasi-experimental, UK office.
Indoor plants in office -> Improved perceived creativity (p<0.05, n=40). ~2 plants per person.
Indoor plants in office -> Improved perceived productivity (p<0.05, n=40).
Plant removal from office -> Increased perceived stress (p<0.05, n=40). Removal effects significant.
Plants in break-out spaces -> No effect on perceived performance (NULL, n=40). Location matters: office yes, break-out no.
Indoor plants in office -> No effect on perceived health, tiredness, motivation, or wellbeing (NULL, n=40).

b_abstract_10.1089/eco.2020.0043_1.content: Virtual nature (video/audio of forests, mountains, streams, ocean) -> Decreased cortisol and GSR in incarcerated adult males. Participants reported feeling calmer, less anxious, less depressed. Mode (audio vs visual) affected some stress indicators differently.

b_abstract_10.1089/eco.2020.0043_2.content: Nature stimuli exposure -> Increased interest in learning about depicted habitats. Different natural habitats elicited different stress responses. Supports nature-based interventions for nature-deprived populations.

b_abstract_10.1093/ajcn/23.7.868_1.content: Daylight design in hospital wards -> Visual comfort NOT achieved when glare present and daylight factor < 1% at bed-head. Malaysian hospital parametric study.

b_abstract_10.1093/ajcn/23.7.868_2.content: Daylight vs solar heat gain trade-off -> Must balance visual comfort with thermal comfort. Luminance ratio > 10 causes unacceptable glare.

b_abstract_10.1109/AERO53065.2022.984327.content: Biophilic design elements in space habitat -> Increased feelings of calm, ease, satisfaction, relaxation, contentment (p<0.05, n=6). VR simulation of ISS crew quarters.
Biophilic design elements in space habitat -> Reduced feelings of tension, strain, nervousness, discomfort (p<0.05, n=6). VR simulation.
Biophilic design elements in space habitat -> No effect on heart rate (NULL finding, n=6). Subjective benefits without physiological change.

b_abstract_10.1109/access.2020.3048737_1.content: Digital interface layout + gender -> Significant gender differences in cognition (behavioral + NIRS) for 3-4 element combinations. HbO concentration differentially activated by gender. H-type (4 elements) and left-I-type (3 elements) showed positive emotion orientation differences.

b_abstract_10.1109/icassp.2014.6854525_1.content: Bipolar disorder mood states -> Detectable from unstructured daily cellular phone conversations. Manic and depressive states recognizable from speech patterns. Supports continuous unobtrusive wellness monitoring feasibility.

b_abstract_10.1111/ina.12387_1.content: Low ventilation (2.3 L/s vs 28.2 L/s per person, CO2 2260 vs 540 ppm) -> Weak negative effect on information retrieval task performance (n=36, 4hr exposure). No effects on health symptoms. Increased subjective fatigue and perceived heat impairment.

b_abstract_10.1121/1.4708896_1.content: Attention focus on sound sources -> Modulates overall soundscape evaluation via cocktail-party effect. Can deliberately attract attention to positive sources for design.

b_abstract_10.1126/science.adp2241_1.content: Adequate ventilation -> Reduced airborne pathogen transmission risk. COVID-19 pandemic revealed ventilation undervalued in public health. Review emphasizes ventilation as infection control measure.

b_abstract_10.1152/physiol.2025.40.s1.09.content: Heat stress (50°C) + 90min cognitive task -> Significantly greater increases in rectal temp (+0.7°C), skin temp (+3.5°C), HR (+19 bpm) vs thermoneutral. Also increased fatigue, decreased vigor, worse thermal comfort (n=7).

b_abstract_10.1177/0013916517738077_1.content: Low 'warm' lighting -> Slowest responses in inhibition, working memory, facial expression recognition tasks (n=60). Low 'cool' lighting induced least positive mood. High 'cool' best for afternoon long-term memory.

b_abstract_10.1186/s12877-025-05713-2_1.content: Indoor ventilation frequency -> Better cognitive function in elderly (β=0.14, p<0.01, n=10,372). Chinese longitudinal study.

b_abstract_10.1186/s12877-025-05713-2_2.content: Ventilation frequency -> Reduced anxiety -> Better self-rated health -> Better cognition. Chain mediation pathway confirmed.

b_abstract_10.1186/s12889-021-11853-y_1.content: Road traffic noise -> Lower executive function in older adults (Animal Naming Test, n=1706, Ireland). May be confounded by air pollution.

b_abstract_10.1186/s12889-021-11853-y_2.content: Road traffic noise -> No effect on memory in older adults (NULL, n=1706).

b_abstract_10.1186/s12889-021-11853-y_3.content: Road traffic noise -> No effect on processing speed in older adults (NULL, n=1706).

b_abstract_10.1371/journal.pmed.1004001_.content: School-outdoor road traffic noise -> Slower working memory development in children (-4.83 points per 5 dB, p<0.001, n=2680). Barcelona longitudinal cohort.
Classroom noise level -> Greater inattentiveness (+2.49 ms RT per 5 dB, p=0.050, n=2680). Children ages 7-10.
Noise fluctuation events at school -> Slower cognitive development (-4.38 per 50 events, p=0.002, n=2680). Fluctuation more predictive than average levels.
Home road traffic noise -> No effect on working memory or attention (NULL finding, n=2680). School exposure matters, home does not.

b_abstract_10.1371/journal.pone.0307934_.content: Indoor biophilic greening (Japanese vs tropical design) -> Both improve impressions vs control. Japanese design more effective at decreasing negative emotions. Tropical design promotes positive mood states. No effect on HRV or cognitive task performance.
Indoor office greening (any design) -> Increased neural efficiency during cognitive tasks (EEG). Limited frequency bands and ROIs affected. Mechanism: greenery may reduce cognitive load during tasks.

b_abstract_10.1523/jneurosci.0952-09.200.content: Visual short-term memory search -> N2pc elicited when identifying targets in VSTM representation, similar to perceptual search (EEG). Spatially specific neural mechanisms overlap between perceptual and memory domains.

b_abstract_10.1523/jneurosci.1455-20.202.content: Selective attention in cocktail party -> Enhanced phonetic feature encoding for attended speech (EEG, n=14). Acoustic feature encoding NOT differentially affected by attention. Supports hierarchical speech processing model.

b_abstract_10.15627/jd.2024.22_1.content: Parametric patterned facade daylight -> Improved spatial ability task performance in architecture students. Experimental, paired-sample.

b_abstract_10.15627/jd.2024.22_2.content: Parametric patterned facade daylight -> Reduced negative affect (PANAS) in architecture students.

b_abstract_10.17645/up.v6i1.3481_1.content: Urban tree removal -> +5°C PET increase (outdoor thermal comfort). Munich simulation study. Tree preservation has greatest thermal impact.

b_abstract_10.17645/up.v6i1.3481_2.content: Parking space reduction -> Enables tree retention -> Better outdoor thermal comfort. Trade-off between mobility and microclimate.

b_abstract_10.17660/actahortic.2010.881..content: [REVIEW] Indoor plants -> Remove air pollutants (formaldehyde, CO, benzene, toluene, ozone) via root bacteria. Scales to whole-building level.
[REVIEW] Indoor plants -> Raise relative humidity (+5% RH) and reduce particulates (20%). Physical air quality benefits.
[REVIEW] Indoor plants -> Reduced stress, faster recovery, reduced mental fatigue, higher productivity. Multiple cited studies.

b_abstract_10.18178/ijscer.12.3.99-105_1.content: Biophilic design in health facilities -> Can address stress, lack of concentration, fatigue, decreased performance. Hybrid approach combining biophilic design + BIM proposed. Checklist developed for assessing biophilic patterns.

b_abstract_10.18666/jpra-2016-v34-i3-689.content: Natural sounds exposure -> Better cognitive task performance than silence (approaching significance). Supports Attention Restoration Theory. Lab experiment.

b_abstract_10.20965/jrm.2021.p0784_1.content: Robotic pet (PARO) interaction -> Reduced behavioral/psychological symptoms of dementia (DBD-13) in elderly with cognitive impairment. Symptoms increased during PARO-absent periods. Staff workload also reduced.

b_abstract_10.21608/ijarpsd.2018.183093_.content: [FRAMEWORK] Sustainability alone does not guarantee occupant satisfaction. Restorative Environmental Design = Sustainable + Biophilic.

b_abstract_10.23919/CCC55666.2022.990214.content: Thermal sensation recognition from posture (BI-LSTM, skeleton data) -> 86.9% accuracy for 7-category thermal sensation. Camera-based non-invasive method feasible for intelligent environmental control in offices.

b_abstract_10.25144/14148_1.content: Sound system design at large musical events -> Audience subconscious auditory responses should inform metrics. Understanding audience expectations vs technology limitations important. Cognitive psychology and neuroscience approaches recommended.

b_abstract_10.33564/ijeast.2022.v06i10.0.content: [REVIEW] Biophilic design in transitional educational spaces -> Stress reduction, productivity, attentiveness, calmness, mental restoration. Literature review noting gap in higher education research.

b_abstract_10.3389/fnhum.2019.00386_1.content: Multi-speaker environment (VR cafe): ~30% of participants frequently shifted gaze to distractors regardless of audiovisual distraction severity (eye-tracking study). Gaze shifts negatively impacted target speech comprehension.

b_abstract_10.3389/fnhum.2019.00386_2.content: Gaze shifts between competing speakers occur primarily during gaps in acoustic input ('glimpsing'). Individual differences in gaze pattern during selective attention to speech. Supports momentary reductions in masking prompting attention shifts.

b_abstract_10.3389/fnhum.2025.1549824_1.content: Complex construction noise vs steady noise -> Worse accuracy and reaction time (EEG + behavioral study). Complex noise disrupts cognitive processing due to unpredictability. Workers develop some adaptation to continuous noise.

b_abstract_10.3389/fnhum.2025.1549824_2.content: High construction noise levels (regardless of type) -> Significant declines in attention, increased mental stress and mental fatigue. Steady noise induces greater fatigue/stress than complex at high levels.

b_abstract_10.3389/fphys.2025.1700518_1.content: [SYSTEMATIC REVIEW, 124 studies] Biophilic elements in confined settings -> Reduced stress, improved mood, faster recovery. Supports SRT and ART.

b_abstract_10.3389/fphys.2025.1700518_2.content: [SYSTEMATIC REVIEW] Plant modules in space habitats -> Support cognitive function and psychological resilience. Applicable to hospitals, eldercare, space.

b_abstract_10.3389/fpsyg.2017.02093_1.content: Urban public squares (30min exposure) -> Significant increase in cognitive performance and decrease in negative affect (n=46, field study). Effect size varied by square restorative potential. Cities can be restorative.

b_abstract_10.3389/fpsyg.2018.01583_1.content: Indoor physical features (air quality, light) -> Hedonic wellbeing in LEED Gold office (n=213). Cross-sectional survey.

b_abstract_10.3389/fpsyg.2018.01583_2.content: Indoor social features (privacy) -> Prevents negative wellbeing (n=213). Green building Canada.

b_abstract_10.3389/fpsyg.2018.01583_3.content: Combined indoor environmental features -> Eudaimonic wellbeing (n=213). Physical + social equally important.

b_abstract_10.3389/fpsyg.2018.01583_4.content: Person-environment fit + pro-environmental behavior + social belonging mediate indoor features -> wellbeing relationship.

b_abstract_10.3390/app14219798_1.content: ICU window design: 25% window-to-wall ratio optimal for daylight autonomy and circadian stimulus autonomy. Centered windows preferred for uniform distribution. Bright interior coatings recommended.

b_abstract_10.3390/ijerph121114709_1.content: Doubling ventilation rate (20→40 cfm/person) -> Improved cognitive performance. Cost <$40 per person per year across 7 US climate zones. With ERV, environmental impact essentially neutralized.

b_abstract_10.3390/ijerph17072271_1.content: Birdsongs in urban parks -> Enhanced perceived mental restoration (Harbin Sun Island). Optimal conditions: sky index 13-36%, tree coverage 30-39%, soft/hard ratio 5-21. Wetland paths showed strongest birdsong effect.

b_abstract_10.3390/su15021144_1.content: Daylighting exposure >1000lx (vs static artificial) -> Reduced sleepiness, increased activity (pilot study, n=17, Stockholm February). Mood and time perception also affected. Supports circadian benefits even at 59°N.

b_abstract_10.3390/su16177778_1.content: Rural elderly thermal comfort (Xi'an summer, n=7 villages): Neutral operative temp 23.9°C, humidity 63.3%, air velocity 0.28 m/s. Comfort ranges: ≤29.3°C (80% acceptability), 43-81% RH, 0.16-0.41 m/s airflow.

b_abstract_10.3390/su16177778_2.content: Rural elderly adaptive model slope larger than standard -> Higher comfort temps in warmer environments. Higher clothing insulation in summer, less temperature sensitive. Reflects prolonged adaptation + low household income constraints.

b_abstract_10.3390/su17219459_1.content: Exterior view evaluation (EVE) -> Strongest predictor of positive mood in classrooms (Random Forest 82% accuracy, SHAP analysis, n=557 middle school students). Higher floors + EVE≥3 associated with positive mood.

b_abstract_10.3390/su17219459_2.content: Optimal classroom lighting for mood: Horizontal desktop illuminance >300lx, frontal eye-level <400lx, left-side 300-1000lx, proximity to windows <2.5m. Field study in 6 classrooms, eastern China.

b_abstract_10.3397/in-2021-1813_1.content: Biophilic sound masking (water, wind, nature sounds) -> Better acoustic comfort AND pleasantness than broadband pink/white noise. Office case study.

b_abstract_10.3397/in_2024_3298_1.content: Park landscape characteristics near expressway -> Influence psychological perception through multi-sensory composite perception. Soundscape theory framework applied to Chengdu wetland park. GIS analysis + sound walks used.

b_abstract_10.3397/in_2024_4248_1.content: ANC headphones alone in office with speech (52 dB) -> No improvement in cognitive performance (visual serial recall, 3-back) or physiological stress (HRV). n=54. Only ANC + masking improved subjective experience.

b_abstract_10.69554/amqu2125_1.content: Indoor air pollutants (PM, VOCs, bioaerosols, CO, NO2, CO2, radon) -> Adverse health effects. Cheap monitoring sensors enable real-time measurement. UK legislation fragmented compared to outdoor air standards.

b_abstract_sha256:0f0ce830ad46_1.content: VR instruction vs paper/pencil -> No significant difference in ergonomic concepts learning, attitudes, or office layout design expertise (NULL, 1996 early VR).

b_abstract_sha256:95e607b517ef_1.content: Air movement -> Cooling benefit in warm conditions via convective heat transfer. But high air movement in cool conditions risks draft discomfort.

b_abstract_sha256:95e607b517ef_2.content: Acceptable air velocity -> Depends on temperature + humidity. ASHRAE thermal comfort standard guidelines.

b_abstract_sha256:f0ac28d766e1_1.content: Assistive listening telecoil mode -> Better speech intelligibility, less listening effort for hearing-impaired students. But reduced environmental awareness.

b_abstract_sha256:f0ac28d766e1_2.content: Combined microphone+telecoil mode -> Best compromise between audibility and awareness for hearing-impaired students in classrooms.

b_abstract_sha256:f0ac28d766e1_3.content: Hearing-impaired students -> Require significantly lower classroom noise and competing speech levels than normal hearing students.

b_ceiling_001.content: High ceilings (10 ft) prime freedom-related concepts, prompting relational processing and abstract/integrated thinking [3 experiments, n=32+100+34, Meyers-Levy & Zhu 2007]

b_ceiling_002.content: Low ceilings (8 ft) prime confinement-related concepts, prompting item-specific processing and concrete/discrete thinking [3 experiments, Meyers-Levy & Zhu 2007]

b_ceiling_003.content: Ceiling height effects on cognition require salience (awareness of ceiling); when not salient, effects are absent [experimental, Meyers-Levy & Zhu 2007]

b_ceiling_004.content: High ceilings facilitate relational elaboration: identifying more shared dimensions among items, more abstract dimensions, fewer subgroups per dimension [n=100, Meyers-Levy & Zhu 2007]

b_ceiling_005.content: High ceilings lead to greater recall clustering (indicator of relational processing); low ceilings lead to better cued recall (indicator of item-specific processing) [n=34, Meyers-Levy & Zhu 2007]

b_ceiling_006.content: Ceiling height effects on processing type are not mediated by mood - no differences in positive or negative affect between high and low ceiling conditions [Meyers-Levy & Zhu 2007]

b_ceiling_007.content: High ceilings → increased beauty judgments; activated left precuneus and left middle frontal gyrus (visuospatial processing regions) [fMRI, n=18, Vartanian et al. 2015]

b_ceiling_008.content: High ceilings affect beauty judgments but NOT approach-avoidance decisions (enter/exit) - dissociation between aesthetic preference and behavioral intention [fMRI, n=18, Vartanian et al. 2015]

b_ceiling_009.content: Open rooms (high visual/locomotive permeability) → more beautiful judgments AND more enter decisions [fMRI, n=18, Vartanian et al. 2015]

b_ceiling_010.content: Enclosed rooms → more exit decisions; activated anterior midcingulate cortex (aMCC) - region with direct amygdala projections involved in fear processing [fMRI, n=18, Vartanian et al. 2015]

b_ceiling_011.content: Precuneus activation with high ceilings is related to beauty ratings - visuospatial exploration contributes to aesthetic preference for higher ceilings [fMRI, Vartanian et al. 2015]

b_ceiling_012.content: Open spaces activated superior and middle temporal gyri during beauty judgments - regions involved in temporal dynamics of visual processing and motion representation [fMRI, Vartanian et al. 2015]

b_spatial_001.content: Presence of objects in room → increased subjective creative performance [VR study, n=participants]

b_spatial_002.content: Room size has no significant effect on objective creativity measures [VR study, n=participants]

b_spatial_003.content: Reverberation increases perceived room size compared to anechoic conditions [experimental, n=15]

b_spatial_004.content: Even weak reverberation cues provide room-size spatial information for blind/VI individuals [experimental, n=10]

b_spatial_005.content: Sites with high prospect (openness) AND refuge (protection) are more preferred than other configurations [field study, n=129]

b_spatial_006.content: Perceived openness (prospect) is significant predictor of environmental preference [field study, n=129]

b_spatial_007.content: Perceived disturbance from background buildings negatively affects landscape preferences [field study, n=129]

b_spatial_008.content: Prospect (visual openness) positively affects preference in urban and interior environments [meta-analysis]

b_spatial_009.content: Both prospect AND refuge contribute to comfort in natural environments [meta-analysis]

b_spatial_010.content: Moderate spatial complexity in interiors is preferred over minimal or excessive complexity [meta-analysis]

b_spatial_011.content: High prospect + low refuge natural environments → restorative (stress/fatigue recovery) [n=269 survey + n=34 experiment]

b_spatial_012.content: Low prospect + high refuge natural environments (dense woods) → increased stress and attention fatigue [n=34 experiment]

b_spatial_013.content: Dense wooded areas low in prospect may evoke fear and require directed attention, blocking restoration [n=34 experiment]

b_spatial_014.content: Higher ceiling heights provide prospect (visual openness/overview) [theoretical, Hildebrand 1991]

b_spatial_015.content: Lower ceiling heights provide refuge (sense of enclosure/protection) [theoretical, Hildebrand 1991]

b_spatial_016.content: Balance of prospect and refuge characteristics in architectural design affects sense of security and wellbeing [theoretical]

b_edge_daylight_warmth_1.content: Higher daylight illuminance levels (600-1400 lx vs 130 lx) increase perceived thermal warmth in indoor environments, independent of actual air temperature. Controlled experiment with 3 daylight × 3 temperature conditions.

b_edge_daylight_restorativeness_1.content: Natural daylight in indoor environments promotes psychological restoration, with 42% of relationships in a systematic review of 33 studies showing positive restorative effects. Direct sunlight without discomfort is most effective.

b_edge_wood_warmth_1.content: Wood surfaces are perceived as the warmest interior material. Natural wood color reflects yellow-red spectrum wavelengths associated with heat. Perceived warmth increases with wood coverage up to medium levels, following an inverse U relationship.

b_edge_noise_cognitive_load_1.content: High noise levels (51 LAeq dB) significantly impair working memory performance compared to low noise (39 LAeq dB). Intelligible background speech causes 8-10% decrease in cognitively demanding tasks.

b_edge_warmth_satisfaction_1.content: Perceived warmth and thermal comfort are defined as psychological states of satisfaction with the thermal environment (ASHRAE). Thermal comfort/warmth plays a significant role in determining occupants' overall satisfaction with indoor environments.

b_edge_cognitive_load_stress_1.content: As cognitive tasks progress, participants exhibit significant increases in mental fatigue, mental effort, and mental stress. Cognitive overload (when information exceeds capacity) leads to stress and frustration.

b_edge_cognitive_load_focus_1.content: Higher cognitive load can decrease distractibility by suppressing peripheral processing. When task difficulty is high, people make compensatory shifts in concentration, making attention more steadfast. Complex bidirectional relationship.

b_edge_crowding_stress_1.content: Higher social density is associated with negative emotions, reduced cognitive task performance, and elevated psychological and physiological stress. Crowding triggers fight-or-flight through sensory overload and loss of perceived control.

b_theory_art.content: Attention Restoration Theory (ART): Natural environments restore directed attention capacity through soft fascination and being away from demands

b_theory_srt.content: Stress Recovery Theory (SRT): Natural environments trigger parasympathetic activation, reducing stress through evolutionary affiliation with nature

b_theory_biophilia.content: Biophilia Hypothesis: Humans have an innate tendency to seek connections with nature and other forms of life, with psychological benefits

b_theory_prospect_refuge.content: Prospect-Refuge Theory: Humans prefer environments that offer both prospect (open views for surveillance) and refuge (protected spaces for safety)

b_theory_ceiling_priming.content: Ceiling Height Priming Theory: High ceilings prime freedom-related concepts promoting relational processing; low ceilings prime confinement promoting item-specific processing
